sample.ans:
In 1831, English scientist Michael Faraday discovered that when the magnetic flux linking a conductor changes, an e.m.f is induced in the conductor. This phenomenon is known as electromagnetic induction.
The interplay of electric and magnetic forces is the basis for electric motors, generators, and many other modern technologies.

In a crystalline solid, the particles (ion, molecule or atoms) are arranged in definite geometric pattern in the three dimensional network. This is known as long range order. This arrangement repeats periodically over the entire crystal. Due to this arrangement, they have short range as well as long range order.
Crystals have smooth faces and straight edges. When a crystal is broken, it cleaves along certain preferred directions. Quartz, Sucrose (sugar), diamond and rock salt (NaCl) are examples of solids that occur as large size single crystals. Structure of NaCl crystal is shown in Fig.16.1.
POLYCRYSTALLINE SOLIDS Polycrystalline is a material made up of many small single crystals (also called crystallites or grains). Polycrystalline solids consist of fine grains, having a size of 10" A to 10 A°, separated by well define boundaries and oriented in different directions. Each such grain is a single crystal of an irregular shape.
Since the grains are oriented haphazardly, a polycrystalline material is isotropic and exhibits the same properties in all directions. Metals are examples of polycrystalline solids. In these solids the ordered regions, vary in size and orientation with respect to one another.
These regions are called as grains (domain) and are separated from one another by grain boundaries as shown in Fig. 16.2. The atomic order can vary from one domain to the next. The grains are usually 100 nm-100 microns in diameter.
Amorphous (Non-crystalline) solid is composed of randomly orientated atoms, ions, or molecules that do not form defined patterns or lattice structures. So in amorphous solids the arrangement of atoms is random. These are the substance whose constituent particles don't possess a regular orderly arrangement. Some liquids when cooled become more and more viscous and then rigid, retaining random atom characteristic distribution. This state is called under cooled liquid or amorphous solid. Glass, rubber, glues and most of polymers are examples of amorphous solids. The atomic arrangement of the three classes of solids is illustrated in Fig. 16.3

To ask a question or a series of questions form many people in order to gather information is called survey. When every individual of the population is examined, it is called population survey or census and if only a part of the population is examined, it is called sample survey or sampling survey. Nowadays. sample surveys are being widely used by government departments like agriculture, industries, commerce etc. and private agencies for obtaining estimates of respective parameters. Sample survey has two types i.e. descriptive sample. survey (simple information are obtained) and analytical sample survey (comparisons are made between subgroups of the population).
Before applying any sampling procedure, it is essential to have a list of all the sampling units or a map or other acceptable material which represent the population to be covered. Such a list or map is called sampling frame. For example, if we wish to estimate the wheat crop area in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the record of farms along with the names of the farmers, villages etc. are the frame. sample.q: Describe the structure of human respiratory system.
steps: Follow the air path: nostrils and nasal cavities → pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli.
Describe the nose: hairs, mucus and cilia filter air; a blood supply warms it and mucus moistens it.
Describe the conducting passages: pharynx is shared with the digestive tract; the larynx has vocal cords; cartilage supports the trachea and bronchi.
Describe the branching passages: two bronchi enter the lungs, divide repeatedly and form bronchioles, which lack cartilage and open into alveoli.
Describe the exchange surfaces: thin moist alveolar epithelium, capillary networks and a large area support diffusion; elastic fibres allow expansion and recoil.
Locate the lungs: the right has three lobes, the left two; pleural membranes surround them and their bases rest on the diaphragm.

  6. Locate the lungs: the right has three lobes, the left two; pleural membranes surround them and their bases rest on the diaphragm.

sample.q: Explain the working of feedback system in a living body and compare it with a non-living physical feedback system.
steps: Name the three components: a receptor detects change, a control centre compares information with a set point, and an effector produces a response.
